Expand Site and Survey Covariates into GDR Intervals

Source: R/expand_gdr_intervals.R
expand_gdr_intervals.Rd

Copy chosen site covariates, or covariates recorded once per visit, into the observation table of an unmarkedFrameGDR, which has one row per survey and removal interval. A removal formula reads its covariates from that table, so a covariate constant within a survey, such as the observer, must be repeated there before you can use it in the removal formula. The function also adds the interval number and returns a copy of the frame with a record of how every row was aligned.

Usage

expand_gdr_intervals(
  object,
  event_keys,
  event_id,
  interval_units,
  site_covariates = character(),
  yearly_covariates = character(),
  interval = "interval",
  site_id = NULL,
  effort = NULL,
  expected_event_keys = NULL
)

Arguments

object

An unmarkedFrameGDR with its original counts and its site, yearly and observation covariates.

event_keys

Data frame with one row per survey event, in the frame's order (all primary periods of the first frame row, then the second, and so on). Include completed surveys with zero counts. Use the original survey identifiers.

event_id

Character vector naming the column(s) of event_keys that identify a survey.

interval_units

Character string naming the time unit of the removal intervals, such as "minutes". Interval lengths are kept, not converted.

site_covariates

Character vector naming the site covariates (siteCovs) to repeat. The default is none. Name an element to give the copy a new name, for example c(rem_forest = "forest", rem_observer = "Observer"). Unnamed elements keep the source name. Nothing is inferred from model formulas, so list every covariate you need.

yearly_covariates

Character vector naming covariates in the frame's yearly table (yearlySiteCovs, one row per primary period) to repeat, with the same naming convention. The default is none. Despite the name, these rows are primary periods (visits), not necessarily years.

interval

Character string, default "interval". The name of the new column holding the interval number (1, 2, ...). It must differ from the event keys and from the other new columns.

site_id

Optional column(s) of event_keys that identify the physical site, passed to prepare_gdr_intervals() and validate_unmarked_data().

effort

Optional numeric vector of survey effort, one value per event, passed to validate_unmarked_data(). Positive values mark completed surveys, zero marks unsurveyed events and NA marks unknown effort.

expected_event_keys

Optional independent event list in frame order, passed to validate_unmarked_data().

Value

A list of class msr_gdr_intervals, as from prepare_gdr_intervals(): data is the copied frame with the new observation columns, survey_audit is the survey audit, alignment records which input row fills each observation row, and protocol records units, interval lengths and the added columns. In addition, protocol$expanded_covariates is a data frame with one row per copied covariate: source_table ("site" or "yearly"), the source column and its target name in the observation table. With no covariates selected, only the interval column is added. fit_eligibility_established is always FALSE.

Why repeat covariates

When the removal formula contains a random effect, unmarked evaluates the random-effect part on the observation table, and that step also needs the formula's fixed covariates there. Repeating only an observer label can therefore leave a formula such as ~ rem_forest + I(interval == 1) + (1 | rem_observer) without rem_forest. Select every survey-constant covariate the observation formula needs.

How values are repeated

A site covariate is repeated for every primary period and interval at that site. A yearly covariate is repeated only for the intervals of its own primary period. Column classes, matrix columns, factor levels, contrasts and missing values are kept. Nothing is standardized, imputed or dropped, and the original covariate tables, counts, distance bands and interval lengths are unchanged. Existing observation columns cannot be overwritten. For covariates that change from one interval to the next, use prepare_gdr_intervals() directly.

Name copies by role

Give a copy a new name when the same field plays different roles, for example forest in the abundance formula and rem_forest in the removal formula. A copy holds the values present when it was made. If you later change the site covariate, for example while estimating its scale of effect, the copy does not change with it. multiScale_optim() also stops if a covariate whose scale it estimates shares its name with a column in the observation or yearly tables, so new names avoid that conflict.

Aligning the data does not show that a model fitted to it converges or that its parameters are identifiable. See the "Add covariates for the time intervals" section of vignette("v12-distance-removal", package = "multiScaleR") for a worked example.

See also

prepare_gdr_intervals(), prepare_gdr_histories(), validate_unmarked_data()

Examples

# Two surveys, two distance bands and three removal intervals
frame <- unmarked::unmarkedFrameGDR(matrix(0, 2, 2), matrix(0, 2, 3),
  siteCovs = data.frame(forest = c(.2, .8), Observer = factor(c("A", "B"))),
  dist.breaks = c(0, 25, 75), unitsIn = "m", period.lengths = c(1, 2, 1))
keys <- data.frame(survey = c("s1", "s2"))
# Copy forest and observer into the interval table under new names
prepared <- expand_gdr_intervals(frame, keys, "survey", "minutes",
  site_covariates = c(rem_forest = "forest", rem_observer = "Observer"))
# One row per survey and interval, ready for a removal formula such as
# ~ rem_forest + I(interval == 1) + (1 | rem_observer)
unmarked::obsCovs(prepared$data)
#>   interval rem_forest rem_observer
#> 1        1        0.2            A
#> 2        2        0.2            A
#> 3        3        0.2            A
#> 4        1        0.8            B
#> 5        2        0.8            B
#> 6        3        0.8            B
prepared$protocol$expanded_covariates
#>   source_table   source       target
#> 1         site   forest   rem_forest
#> 2         site Observer rem_observer
